comparisons.peer_summary: The company's strategy focuses on technology leadership in semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, achieved through strategic acquisitions and internal R&D to maintain market leadership and drive diversified financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom describe a strategy focused on technology leadership in the data center and infrastructure markets, but they emphasize different mechanisms. AMD highlights accelerating growth through specific product launches (MI300X GPUs and EPYC CPUs) and an annual roadmap cadence. Broadcom emphasizes achieving leadership through a combination of strategic acquisitions and internal R&D to maintain a comprehensive suite of products.

sentences.text: One of our priorities in 2024 was to accelerate growth in our Data Center segment.
During the year, we announced that we have accelerated our AMD AI accelerator roadmap to deliver an annual cadence of leadership AMD Instinct solutions.

Our strategy is focused on technology leadership and category-leading semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions delivering a comprehensive suite of innovative infrastructure technology products to the world's leading business and government customers.

We seek to achieve this through strategic acquisitions of businesses and technologies, as well as extensive internal research and development, to ensure our products retain their technology market leadership.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel launched Intel Xeon 6 processors for data centers using Intel 3 process and Efficient cores, designed to address diverse workload deployments. The 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors, based on Intel 7, continued to ramp throughout 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose specific Data Center CPU product launches and roadmaps for 2024. AMD announced the 5th Gen AMD EPYC family and accelerated its AI accelerator roadmap to an annual cadence. Intel launched Intel Xeon 6 processors utilizing the Intel 3 process and Efficient cores, while continuing to ramp 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors. Both companies frame these launches as responses to diverse data center workload demands.

sentences.text: We announced our 5th Gen AMD EPYC™ family of server processors, providing leadership performance and capabilities for a wide range of data center workloads.
During the year, we announced that we have accelerated our AMD AI accelerator roadmap to deliver an annual cadence of leadership AMD Instinct solutions.

▪Data center CPUs. We launched our Intel® Xeon® 6 processors for the data center, utilizing the Intel 3 process, including our first Intel Xeon processor using Efficient cores (E-cores). The Intel Xeon 6 family is designed to address the growing diversity in workloads and deployments in the data center environments. Our 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors, based on Intel 7, were launched in 2023, and continued to ramp throughout 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: CNBU data center sales were driven by server demand in cloud and enterprise markets, with growth fueled by the shift of infrastructure and workloads to the cloud and the memory-intensive nature of AI data-centric workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron identify strong demand from hyperscaler and cloud customers for data center products driven by AI workloads. AMD reports very strong demand for its AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs deployed by hyperscalers. Micron attributes its data center CNBU sales growth to server demand in cloud and enterprise markets, specifically noting that cloud servers supporting AI and data-centric workloads require significantly increasing quantities of memory (DRAM/HBM).

sentences.text: The demand for our data center AI accelerator products was very strong as large hyperscaler customers, OEMs and ODMs deployed our AMD Instinct™ MI300X GPUs.
Data center: CNBU sales to the data center end market were driven primarily by server demand across the cloud and enterprise markets and solutions offered to the networking market.

Cloud servers supporting AI and data-centric workloads require significantly increasing quantities of DRAM, including HBM, and NAND as the task of turning data into insight becomes increasingly memory-centric.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA extends its AI leadership by providing a complete end-to-end accelerated computing platform for training and inferencing, including GPUs, CPUs, DPUs, DGX Cloud, and NeMo, supported by a large ecosystem of developers and partners.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA focus their data center strategy on AI accelerator and accelerated computing leadership. AMD highlights the strong demand for its AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs and the acceleration of its AI accelerator roadmap. NVIDIA describes its strategy as extending AI leadership through a complete, end-to-end accelerated computing platform for training and inferencing, including GPUs and full-stack solutions. Both companies frame their core growth around providing comprehensive AI infrastructure solutions.

sentences.text: One of our priorities in 2024 was to accelerate growth in our Data Center segment.
The demand for our data center AI accelerator products was very strong as large hyperscaler customers, OEMs and ODMs deployed our AMD Instinct™ MI300X GPUs.
We provide a complete, end-to-end accelerated computing platform for AI, addressing both training and inferencing.
GPUs are uniquely suited to AI, and we will continue to add AI-specific features to our GPU architecture to further extend our leadership position.
